channel.title: Nolan Kido | Practical AI writing
channel.description: Essays, worked guides and recorded cases about practical AI, checking results, and human judgment. Tools and website edits are not new articles.

item.title: Using AI to check continuity across a book series.
item.description: Explore Preflight and canonKeeper through a Sherlock Holmes continuity audit, source passages, correct and incorrect findings, and a transparent benchmark.

item.title: Using AI to turn guidance into a weekly-reset note.
item.description: Inspect a real AI-assisted editing exercise: three public guides, the original draft, five source checks, corrections, and a reusable weekly-reset note.

item.title: Dinner on Time: building a cooking planner with AI.
item.description: See how an AI-assisted cooking planner handles an oven delay, preserves progress, and keeps choices explicit. Recorded app demo with a simulated meal.

item.title: Building a local AI review reply tool.
item.description: Inspect Review Reply Writer, a local AI drafting application for customer reviews. Follow its historical demo, saved-text approval, source records, and limitations.

item.title: What a local AI test actually measured.
item.description: Read a documented Gemma test on an Ubuntu CPU runner: per-case timings, retained failures, configuration, and the difference between model latency and task time.

item.title: Using AI to turn source notes into a checked action list.
item.description: Follow eight public source notes through an actual AI-generated publication checklist. Inspect the prompt, complete output, source checks, and unresolved items.

item.title: How to check an AI answer.
item.description: Check AI answers against sources, recompute calculations, review summaries and test code. Six practical methods, worked examples and a reusable review record.

item.title: Check an AI summary against its source.
item.description: Check an AI summary claim by claim. Compare a fictional source, six annotated problems, and a repaired draft, then use the free source-review checklist.

item.title: Should I use AI for this task?
item.description: Decide whether to use AI, choose a simpler method, or pause. Six questions, clear decision rules, four worked examples, and a free private-use worksheet.

item.title: Let AI do more. Keep the judgment.
item.description: Delegating production is not the same as handing over responsibility. An essay on purpose, boundaries, permission, and the choices worth keeping human.

item.title: Checking an AI-assisted website change.
item.description: A documented AI-assisted website change passed 347 tests but still had malformed HTML. Inspect the repair, reproduce the failure, and reuse the checking method.

item.title: A working tool is not the same as a trustworthy one.
item.description: Two calculations agree. Both are wrong. A small worked example of the difference between a convincing demonstration and independent evidence.
